newsitem.title: UK: Rexam plans to sell some businesses.
newsitem.headline: Rexam plans to sell some businesses.

text.p: Rexam Plc said on Wednesday it was continuing its restructuring and planned to sell a number of businesses that did not fit within its new sectors.
It said the businesses designated for sale had a combined annual turnover of 303 million stg, operating assets of 161 million and an annual operating loss of two million.
The British based industrial materials and packaging group announced in September a disposal programme aimed at getting rid of underperforming business within its widely-spread structure.

The company said at the time that its aim was to point Rexam's overall return on net assets back up towards 25 percent and that the group would restructure into seven sectors each with a clear market focus.
The company has set up a dedicated management team called Rexam Octagon to conduct the disposal programme, led by David Jones as chief executive.

The businesses designated for sale span several sectors -- food and beverages, industrial, beauty, packaging, printing, coated films and paper. Rexam said that at this stage it was inappropriate to speculate about likely proceeds from the sale.
Of the businesses earmarked for sale, the packaging businesses have the largest turnover, at 169 million stg.
Rexam said healthcare and building and engineering were not affected by the disposal plan.

Rexam said the disposals would allow the company's seven sectors to focus specifically on growth opportunities within their markets and that identifying the sale targets would remove speculation about which businesses were to be sold.
In 1996 Rexam sold businesses with a combined annual turnover of 216 million stg and net assets of 77 million stg.
